corrections.text: The article quotes Securities and Futures Commission CEO Julia Leung as saying, "Human review of every intermediate step would be unrealistic." The cited PYMNTS source does not quote her directly; it reports indirectly that Leung "acknowledged that human review of every intermediate step would be unrealistic." The statement reflects PYMNTS' paraphrase, not Leung's verbatim words.

The article quotes Chris Filburn as saying, "liability should lie with whoever is best equipped to prevent the harm or loss in the first place. In this case, it's the AI provider." In the cited PYMNTS source, only the first sentence is a direct quotation, and it begins with the clause "From a legal and policy perspective," which the article omits; the second sentence ("In this case, it's the AI provider") is the reporter's own unquoted summary of Filburn's point, not his verbatim words.

The article describes Anthropic's read-only banking-agent approach as "a contrast point several of these stories flag." Of the five cited sources, only TechCrunch discusses Anthropic; the other four (Decrypt and three PYMNTS pieces) do not mention Anthropic.
